items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This is how we hit upon a group with Norman Simmons, Sweets Edison, and different people that he put together for his group.

ctx.x: What was he doing then? What was . . .?

He was playing clubs and concerts and doing engagements and had a group. He had a group that he was working with. And a lot of times Joe would do things on his own. When I mean on his own, he would just go into a city and work with a local group. He did that for a while. I kept trying to discourage him from that. You need to get a group together where you’ve got to work with. When I met him – first met him – he would work anywhere, all over the country. He’d work with this one or that one or the other one. I…
Did he – he had his own group in the ’80s?

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: So I remember Sweets Edison was in the group

ctx.x: That’s great. When you first started working with Joe then, he had come out of that period where he’d had the hit with the Basie band. Was there a conscious decision with you guys at that point where you said okay, I did the big band thing, now I’m ready for a solo career, or did you find a group to play with him or was he kind of freelancing with different bands?

No, no, no, no, no. He went right into, went pretty much right into a group thing, you know. I think it was Junior Mance was one of the first pianists, and then later on he had several different pianists, I can’t recall exactly in what order and who was there. Joe probably told you that story. But it was a conscious effort to put together a group but it was like a small jazz group, because that was what was the popular thing at the time.
